title: Braves acquire Lane Thomas, Bailey Falter from Royals: MLB Trade Grades
content:
Braves get: OF Lane Thomas and LHP Bailey Falter
Royals get: LHP Carter Holton and RHP Lucas Braun

Braves: B+
Royals: A-

Two years ago, the Cleveland Guardians acquired Thomas at this very time and for this very reason: He can hit left-handed pitching. Truth is, Thomas stunk (and was hurt) for much of his time in Cleveland. An OPS of 67. Negative WAR. Things of that nature. But all of that was largely forgiven because of one swing. In Game 5 of the 2024 ALDS, Thomas uncorked a grand slam off of Detroit Tigers lefty ace Tarik Skubal that sent the Guardians through to the ALCS.

That’s why you go get a Lane Thomas at the trade deadline. It’s why he’s been traded in three different Julys and now an August. You don’t want to face a fearsome lefty in the playoffs and fret that you don’t have someone who can put a good at-bat against him.

Thomas can play all three outfield spots, which is helpful but not entirely necessary for the 2026 Braves. What’s far more crucial is that he has a 125 wRC+ against left-handed pitching this season — and a 133 wRC+ against lefties across his big-league career — while other Atlanta outfield options Mauricio Dubón, Mike Yastrzemski, Eli White and Jorge Mateo are all hitting lefties at a below league-average clip.

The Athletic’s Keith Law ranked Braun, 24, as the Braves’ No. 13 prospect before this season. Atlanta drafted him in the sixth round in 2023 and he moved quickly through the organization. He’s pitched 260 2/3 innings at Double A and 62 2/3 innings at Triple A, which is just a lot more experience at the upper levels of the minors than we’re typically seeing these days. Braun has a deep arsenal, though not overpowering stuff. He provides immediate rotation depth to the Royals’ system.

Holton was a second-round pick in 2024 but made only one appearance in the Braves’ system before undergoing Tommy John surgery. He returned to the mound this spring and had a 4.75 ERA in 41 2/3 innings across rookie ball and Low A. It’s a nice return for a rental outfielder and a struggling reliever. Along with the savings of moving Thomas’ and Falters’ salaries, the Royals come away with two arms — one with more certainty, the other with maybe more upside.
